transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: S-Net enterprise and residential broadband support, Umar speaking. How may I direct your call?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Umar. I run an executive recruitment consultancy from my home office in Guildford, and for the past four days, our VoIP SIP softphones have suffered unbearable audio echo, robotic garbling, and complete call drops every single time we speak to high-value executive clients! I am losing thousands of pounds in candidate placement fees and your service is destroying my business reputation!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how critical voice clarity is for your executive recruitment practice, John. Let's look into the latency and VoIP jitter metrics on your broadband line right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Umar, because my business partners and clients think our phones are breaking down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we access the advanced line diagnostic portal, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The address is 45 Highclere Gardens, Guildford, GU1 2TN, and the security PIN is 9031. On my VoIP softphone diagnostic overlay, I am seeing fourteen percent packet loss and eighty-five milliseconds of jitter during active calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, John. I have opened the real-time session telemetry monitor for your Guildford fiber line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what you are experiencing: over the past four days, your home office VoIP softphones have suffered severe voice echo, robotic distortion, and intermittent call disconnects during client meetings, with packet loss reaching fourteen percent and jitter hitting eighty-five milliseconds. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. It sounds like speaking into an empty metal oil drum inside a tunnel, and our callers constantly complain that our words get chopped into robotic syllables every few seconds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me on hold for about forty-five seconds while I run a sustained packet buffer test from our exchange concentrator.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, John. The packet buffer test shows significant upstream bufferbloat occurring whenever large background file uploads coincide with real-time SIP voice packets, pushing latency spikes over one hundred and twenty milliseconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So background computer data traffic and cloud file syncing is choking the telephone voice packets on the router?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, without Quality of Service prioritization enabled on the gateway, standard bulk TCP data packets contend equally with UDP real-time voice packets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why wasn't Quality of Service prioritization turned on automatically by S-Net when we signed up for your premium fiber package?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Residential fiber gateways ship with default carrier-grade NAT and unprioritized best-effort traffic scheduling across all LAN switch ports, treating high-bandwidth video streams and tiny VoIP UDP voice frames identically.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You market this package as Ultra-Fast Home Worker Fiber! If you sell it to home workers, it should prioritize voice communications out of the box!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well John, running a commercial telephone brokerage over a cheap residential broadband line without buying a dedicated commercial QoS trunk is bound to sound terrible.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Cheap residential line?! I pay sixty-five pounds a month for your top-tier package! How dare you insult my business and call my connection cheap when your service is failing to deliver basic voice packets! That is extraordinarily rude!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I apologize if my phrasing was blunt, John. I am explaining that commercial SIP trunks require dedicated bandwidth reservations under telecom industry standards.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What can S-Net do right now to eliminate this echo and jitter on my line?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can remotely reconfigure your Hub 5 gateway profile from our backend ACS server to enable SIP Differentiated Services Code Point tagging with strict priority queuing for UDP port 5060 and RTP voice streams.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How does DSCP tagging prevent background computer backups from interfering with live voice calls?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: DSCP tagging marks voice packets with Expedited Forwarding Class 46 and maps them directly to IEEE 802.1p priority level 5 on the WAN egress queue, instructing the router to transmit audio packets ahead of all bulk TCP traffic.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will that reduce the eighty-five millisecond jitter back down to normal levels for multi-party conference calls?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, jitter will drop from eighty-five milliseconds down to under five milliseconds, and voice packet loss will be eliminated across both incoming and outgoing channels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds like the exact technical fix we need for our candidate interview panels.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will push the ACS QoS provisioning script to your gateway immediately, which takes approximately thirty seconds to commit to firmware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Go ahead and push the script while I keep my softphone application open on my monitor.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The QoS profile is successfully applied to your Hub 5 gateway and verified in the active routing table.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me run a quick test call on my softphone to my colleague's mobile... the echo is completely gone, and the audio sounds crystal clear!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am glad to hear that the DSCP voice prioritization immediately resolved the audio degradation and packet loss.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is a huge improvement for our day-to-day recruiting operations.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To eliminate any local radio frequency interference on your softphone workstation, I will also dispatch a complimentary ten-meter Cat6 shielded Ethernet cable so you can hardwire your office PC directly to LAN port 1.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is the cable foil-shielded to stop electrical interference from our multiple office monitors and power supplies?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it is a fully screened twisted-pair S/FTP cable with molded snagless boots and internal aluminum shielding to prevent common-mode electrical noise.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A ten-meter shielded cable will let me run a clean wired connection right around the skirting board.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Cat6 cable is dispatched via first-class Royal Mail and will arrive on Friday morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, that will make the office setup rock solid.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will also credit your broadband account with twenty pounds to compensate for the business disruption over the past four days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Twenty pounds credit is very fair and appreciated.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you repeat what packet loss percentage and jitter figures you measured earlier?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you earlier, packet loss was fourteen percent and jitter was eighty-five milliseconds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, John. I am logging fourteen percent packet loss and eighty-five milliseconds jitter into the QoS performance ticket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, glad you have that logged.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The priority QoS reconfiguration reference number on your account ledger is QOS-44019-J, and the active session profile will persist through all future automated firmware upgrades.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Noted down... QOS-44019-J.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Cat6 dispatch consignment reference is CBL-99182-M.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Noted down as well... CBL-99182-M.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How is your overall internet browsing speed performing on non-voice devices like tablets and smart televisions?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Non-voice web browsing has always been blazingly fast, we get nine hundred megabits on our desktop and streaming movies never buffer, so general data speed is superb.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We are pleased that your multi-gigabit fiber download performance remains exceptional and delivers full bandwidth to your Surrey premises.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, streaming and file downloads have been fantastic.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The QoS traffic rules will ensure that high-speed downloads never interfere with softphone audio in future.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait Umar, if my colleague sets up a second softphone on another laptop in our office, will the QoS rule cover both...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The QoS policy is locked and the Cat6 cable is dispatched. Have a good day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait Umar, what about the second laptop... hello?
